channel.title: Get Paid UK tips from NexusAI t/a CastilliAI
channel.description: Short, practical notes on getting paid and chasing late invoices, for UK sole traders and freelancers. This is general information, not legal advice.

item.title: Late payment compensation: the £40, £70 or £100 fixed sum
item.description:
If a business customer pays your invoice late, GOV.UK says you can also charge a fixed sum for the cost of recovering the debt, on top of statutory interest.

The amount depends on the size of the debt: £40 for up to £999.99, £70 for £1,000 to £9,999.99, and £100 for £10,000 or more. You can only charge it once for each payment. If you are the supplier, you can also claim reasonable costs each time you try to recover the debt.

Interest is separate: 8% plus the reference rate, which is 11.75% for interest that starts to run between 1 July and 31 December 2026. This is for business-to-business invoices only. It is general information, not legal advice.

Work out what you can add with the free late payment calculator, or see the Get Paid UK kit for chase templates and a tracker.

item.title: Don’t use today’s Bank Rate for late-invoice interest
item.description:
If a business customer pays you late, you may be able to add statutory interest at 8% plus the official reference rate — not whichever Bank Rate happens to be in force today.

For interest that starts to run between 1 July and 31 December 2026, that reference rate is the Bank of England rate in force on 30 June: 3.75%. So the statutory rate is 11.75%. A later change in Bank Rate does not alter the figure for this half-year.

This only applies to business-to-business invoices, including public authorities, not to private individuals. Always put a clear due date on the invoice. This is general information, not legal advice.

You can check a late invoice with the free late payment calculator, or see the £39 Get Paid UK kit for chase templates and a tracker.
